lines.english: ...The john...

lines.japanese: ……アレキサンダーの、便所か。
lines.english: ...Alexander’s john.

lines.japanese: ……よし。
lines.english: ...Right.

lines.japanese: よし。
lines.english: Right.

lines.japanese: 俺はゆっくり首を回し、膝に力を入れて便座から立ちあがった。
lines.english: I slowly rolled my neck, braced my knees, and rose from the toilet.

lines.japanese: かさ。
lines.english: Rustle.

lines.japanese: その拍子に、手から何かがこぼれた。目で追うと、足元の床に紙くずが転がっている。どうやら俺は、それを右のこぶしに握っていたみたいだ。
lines.english: Something slipped from my hand as I moved. I followed it down and found a crumpled scrap of paper on the floor at my feet. Apparently I'd been clutching it in my right fist.

lines.japanese: 拾いあげて皺を伸ばしてみる。
lines.english: I picked it up and smoothed out the wrinkles.

lines.japanese: 『今日からアレキサンダーでバイトを始めました』
lines.english: *I started working at Alexander today.*

lines.japanese: 大人ぶった柔らかい筆跡。鷲介の字だ。
lines.english: Soft handwriting trying very hard to look grown-up. Shusuke's.

lines.japanese: 『ちょっぴり遅くなっちゃったけど、初日だから大目に見てね。怒っちゃいやよ。世界が平和でありますように──』
lines.english: *I'm just a teensy bit late, but it's my first day, so be nice. Don't get angry, okay? May peace prevail on Earth—*

lines.japanese: ──ハァト。
lines.english: —with a little heart.

lines.japanese: 「ハートじゃねえだろタコ。こっちのハートは震えねンだよ」
lines.english: “That’s no heart, jackass. Mine sure as hell isn’t moved.”

lines.japanese: 俺は広げた紙くずを丸めた紙くずに戻して、くず箱の底に叩きつけた。
lines.english: I crumpled the scrap back into a ball and slammed it into the bottom of the trash can.

lines.japanese: 怒ってねえよ、呆れてるんだ。そもそも、いまぐだぐだと文句を並べたてたところで≪待機室≫に篭ったあいつの耳にはもう届かない。
lines.english: I wasn't angry. I was fed up. Besides, no litany of complaints I made now would ever reach the guy shut away inside the *Waiting Room*.

lines.japanese: 「クソガキが、近いうち≪面談≫の必要ありだな……」
lines.english: “Damn brat. We’re going to need an *Interview* soon...”

lines.japanese: アレはアレで疲れるから嫌なんだけど。
lines.english: Not that I wanted one. Those things were exhausting in their own way.

lines.japanese: 「めんどくせえ。ブッ殺すぞアノヤロウ」
lines.english: “What a pain in the ass. I'll kill him.”

lines.japanese: 俺はすぐそばの台に置かれていたスポーツバッグを開けて、自分の服を引っぱりだす。
lines.english: I opened the sports bag on a nearby counter and pulled out my own clothes.

lines.japanese: こんなチャラい服、着てられるか。
lines.english: No way in hell was I wearing that flashy crap.

lines.japanese: 便所から出て店の壁時計を見た。１０時５５分。
lines.english: I left the john and checked the restaurant clock. Ten fifty-five.

lines.japanese: あのヤロウ、何がちょっぴりだ。約束の時間を二十五分も過ぎてるじゃねえか。
lines.english: That bastard called this a *teensy bit* late? He was twenty-five minutes past the time we'd agreed on.

lines.japanese: 「どうした鷲介、着替えたのか」
lines.english: “What's this, Shusuke? Changed already?”

lines.japanese: さっさと帰ろうとしたら、厨房から不精髭のおっさんが出てきた。たしか……他の従業員に店長と呼ばれているのを何度か耳にしたことがあった。
lines.english: I was making a quick exit when a stubbled older man emerged from the kitchen. If I remembered right... I'd heard the other employees call him the manager a few times.

lines.japanese: もちろん俺は返事などせず、何も聞こえなかったふりをしてすたすた出口へ向かった。それぞれの知人とは極力接触を避けるのが、俺たちの数多い≪取り決め≫のひとつだ。
lines.english: Naturally, I gave no answer. Pretending I hadn't heard a thing, I strode toward the door. Avoiding one another's acquaintances whenever possible was one of the many terms in our *Agreement*.

lines.japanese: 「おい鷲介、ちょっと待ってくれ」
lines.english: “Hey, Shusuke. Wait a moment.”

lines.japanese: しかし、この場合の「極力」とは「相手に不信感を抱かせない範囲内で」という意味でもある。雇用主の制止を無視するのは、おそらく鷲介にとって問題行動なんだろう。
lines.english: But here, ‘whenever possible’ also meant ‘as long as it didn't arouse suspicion.’ Ignoring his boss when he called him back would probably get Shusuke in trouble.

lines.japanese: 俺はやむを得ず立ちどまった。しかし億劫を感じている表情は隠さなかった。
lines.english: I stopped because I had no choice, though I made no effort to hide my reluctance.

lines.japanese: 「例のアレなんだが──」
lines.english: “About that project—”

lines.japanese: 「──ん？　なんだおまえ、ご機嫌斜めなのか」
lines.english: “—Hm? What's wrong with you? In a bad mood?”

lines.japanese: ほっとけ。俺は無言で首を横に振った。
lines.english: Leave me alone. I shook my head without a word.

lines.japanese: 「そうか。まあいい。例のアレなんだが、試しに来週からお客のいない時間に流してみようと思うのだ。実はすでに、ネットラジオで何度か試験放送は行っていてな」
lines.english: “I see. Well, never mind. About that project: starting next week, I thought we might try airing it while the restaurant is empty. In fact, we've already done several test broadcasts over internet radio.”

lines.japanese: 困った。話が見えない。俺は眉をひそめて耳を前に出した。
lines.english: This was a problem. I had no idea what he was talking about. I frowned and pricked up my ears.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、望月君たちから聞いたんだろう？　アレだ。二重の意味でアイドルタイムだ」
lines.english: “Come now, didn't Mochizuki and the others tell you? You know—the idol hour. Idols for the idle hours.”

lines.japanese: ああ、と言葉にならない音で適当に頷いた。意味なんて分からないが、気の済むまで喋らせてしまおう。
lines.english: I nodded with a vague grunt that might have meant *oh.* I had no idea what he meant, but I might as well let him talk himself out.

lines.japanese: 「うむ。いずれはおまえにも放送作家として協力してもらうからな。そうだな、おもに、俺の読みあげるスタイリッシュトークを作成する仕事だ。原稿料は友人価格で頼むぞ」
lines.english: “Indeed. Sooner or later, you'll be helping us as a broadcast writer. Your principal duty will be composing the stylish monologues I deliver. And since we're friends, I expect a discount.”

lines.japanese: うす、と分かったふりで首を振る。無精髭の店長は口をひん曲げると、鼻からひとつ息を吹いた。
lines.english: I grunted something like *sure* and nodded as though I understood. The stubbled manager twisted his mouth, then snorted.

lines.japanese: 「ふん、なにをふて腐れてる。玉泉トレーナーはそんなに厳しかったか？　まあ、やつはああ見えて優しい子だ。そのうち状況も変わるだろう」
lines.english: “Hmph. What's put you in a sulk? Was Coach Tamaizumi really that hard on you? She may not look it, but she's a kind girl. Things will change in time.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、そんな暗い顔をするのはおまえらしくないぞ鷲介。なに、今日のところはウェイトレスもののビデオでも借りて、下半身の溜飲を下げることだ。じゃあな。お疲れ」
lines.english: “Hahaha! That gloomy face isn't like you, Shusuke. For tonight, rent yourself a waitress video and work out that frustration below the belt. See you. Take care.”

lines.japanese: おっさんの言葉遣いはどこの三文芝居かと思うほどに威圧的だけれども、同時にその目には、プロの格闘家が家族に向けるような強くて優しい光があった。
lines.english: The man’s way of talking was as overbearing as something out of a cheap melodrama. Yet his eyes held the same strong, gentle light a professional fighter might turn on his family.

lines.japanese: 懐かしい、どこかのじいさんみたいな目だ。きっと鷲介が世話になっているんだろう。
lines.english: There was something familiar in those eyes—something that reminded me of an old man I used to know. Shusuke must owe this guy a lot.

lines.japanese: 「……お疲れっす」
lines.english: “...Night.”

lines.japanese: 俺はほとんど口を開けずにつぶやいて、表情を隠すように頭を下げた。
lines.english: I murmured it without really opening my mouth, then lowered my head to hide my face.

lines.japanese: 外ヅラのいい鷲介のことだ。きっとこのおっさんたちと、この空間で、器用に明るい青春ってやつを満喫しているんだろう。
lines.english: Shusuke had always been good at putting on a charming face. No doubt he had found a way to enjoy that bright, wholesome thing people called youth with these guys, in this place.

lines.japanese: 俺はほんの少し嫉妬じみた感情を覚えながら、やつの職場をあとにした。
lines.english: With the faintest touch of something like jealousy, I left his workplace.

lines.japanese: 蛇足だけど、俺がやつの生き方に嫉妬するだなんて、ちょっと前までなら絶対にありえなかった話だ。
lines.english: Call it a needless postscript, but until very recently, the idea that I might envy the way he lived would have been unthinkable.
